key_terms: Removing rows from the current table view through a new snapshot while older snapshots may still reference files containing them.
An Iceberg file that marks rows in existing data files as deleted instead of rewriting those data files, with its own reader compatibility requirements.
A maintenance operation that removes old snapshots from table metadata under a retention rule, after which their files become eligible for cleanup.
A separate operation that deletes files no retained snapshot or active write references. Selecting files by age alone is unsafe.
The policy stating how much table history remains readable, which determines how far back time travel and recovery can reach.

worked_examples.title: Delete one order from the current snapshot
worked_examples.code:
first = table.current_snapshot().snapshot_id
table.delete("id = 1")
current = table.scan().to_arrow()
print(sorted(current["id"].to_pylist()), table.scan(snapshot_id=first).to_arrow().num_rows)
worked_examples.interpretation: The current view lists ids 2 and 3 while the first snapshot still returns three rows, so the order is gone logically but the bytes remain readable through history. For a privacy deletion this is not enough. Track which snapshots still reference the deleted row, and treat the request as complete only after those snapshots are expired and the unreferenced files are removed.

worked_examples.title: Expire the historical snapshot
worked_examples.code:
table.maintenance.expire_snapshots().by_id(first).commit()
print(first in {snapshot.snapshot_id for snapshot in table.snapshots()})
print(sorted(table.scan().to_arrow()["id"].to_pylist()))
worked_examples.interpretation: The membership test prints False and the current ids remain 2 and 3. Expiration removes the snapshot from metadata, so time travel to it now fails, but in the lesson the warehouse files are still on disk afterward. Physical removal depends on cleanup of files no longer referenced by any retained snapshot. Branches or tags that protect a snapshot block its expiration, so check references before promising deletion.

evidence: Complete actual local program with independent expected values and explicit negative checks; distributed-system claims are excluded.
